items.q: What's the core loop for effective Claude Code agents?
items.a: **Plan → build → verify → evolve.** Most people skip planning and verification; Cole spends **more time planning than building**. Sandwich delegation between a spec/success criteria and proof — never "go rip" without them.

"Prove to me it's actually done and working." Use unit tests, rendered PNG review, Playwright/browser automation, or custom harnesses. Without checks ~**65–70%** first-pass; with self-validation harnesses ~**92%**.

items.q: When does a huge context window start hurting quality?
items.a: The **dumb zone** hits around **~250K tokens on Opus 4.8** (Sonnet 4.6 earlier, ~100–125K) despite 1M-token windows. Compact or hand off before quality drops; needle-in-haystack problems worsen there.

items.q: Why shouldn't you dump 20 MCP servers upfront?
items.a: **Attention is scarce.** Skills enable **progressive loading**; front-loading MCP tool schemas burns context. Cole's pattern: **CLI + skill** beats MCP for token efficiency (CRM, GitHub, Arkon).

items.q: What is harness engineering for large work?
items.a: A harness is **LLM + tools + context wrapper**. Chain multiple **fresh sessions** (plan → implement → validate) — the viral baseline is the **Ralph loop**; Cole's open-source **Arkon** is a deterministic multi-session orchestrator.

items.q: Should sub-agents orchestrate the whole project?
items.a: Prefer sub-agents for **research/debate**, not deep orchestration — handoffs between sub-agents are poor. "We want to pick when the AI model works in a workflow, instead of having it **drive the whole thing**."

items.q: Why aren't prompts enough for agent security?
items.a: Assume anything the agent can touch, **it will touch** — Nate's team accidentally emailed an entire list with the wrong discount. Use **scoped keys** and **hooks** for pre-tool guards; prompts are not permissions.

items.q: How do bugs become permanent upgrades?
items.a: After each task, **system evolution** updates CLAUDE.md, skills, or planning docs so failures don't repeat. Session-end hooks can write daily logs and promote to memory.md ("Claude dreaming"). "Every bug becomes a **permanent upgrade**."

items.q: What product-manager habits transfer to directing agents?
items.a: You shape **vision and validation**; the agent implements. Give Claude the **why** during planning (**intent engineering**) so it shapes the how. Use `/btw` for sidecar explanations without polluting main context; treat it like your smartest friend and ask the questions in your head.
